heroHeadline: UN: Nearly 600 Afghan Health Facilities Shut by Funding Cuts as Taliban-NRF Clashes Escalate in Baghlan
heroSubtitle: August 30, 2026 is Day 9,093 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 187 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. The UN said funding cuts have forced the closure of nearly 600 Afghan health facilities this year — over 100 of them child-malnutrition treatment sites — leaving roughly 4 million people without care; 3.7 million Afghan children are now acutely malnourished, including 1 million in severe, life-threatening condition, with the WFP's nutrition programme only 22% funded. In Baghlan province, Taliban forces killed two National Resistance Front commanders in Nahrin district on August 27-28 in a rare operation the NRF itself acknowledged, but local sources say two more people killed the same period in Khost district were civilians whose bodies were mutilated with acid and publicly displayed — an incident Taliban authorities call an NRF operation. Separately, an Islamabad High Court judge questioned whether 87 Afghan students with visa extensions frozen for up to 11 months can even invoke Pakistan's constitutional jurisdiction, remarking that 'we are at war with Afghans.' These developments follow the August 27 IBOs in Bannu, South Waziristan and Khuzdar that killed 11 militants; no new cross-border strikes have occurred since the June 28-29 Chamkani/Gyan/Marawara episode, and no formal ceasefire has been confirmed.
